newsitem.title: USA: NYS Bruno sees serious budget talks in June--paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS Bruno sees serious budget talks in June--paper.

text.p: The New York Senate Majority Leader does not look for serious budget talks until June, saying his Democratic opponent in the Assembly will wait for rent controls to end, the Albany Times Union said on Tuesday.
Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, told the paper that his Democratic opponent was not ready to do a budget until regulations that mainly affect apartments in New York City expire on June 15.
Referring to Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, Bruno said: "I don't think he can get serious about anything until we get close to June 15."

The state's budget was due on April 1, and before the legislature took a two-week spring recess, it approved a six-week interim budget. Bruno expects the legislature to approve another short-term measure when it resumes session during the week of May 5, the paper said.

Bruno also rejected Silver's calls for sending different bills approved by the two houses to conference committees, saying rent control was too emotional an issue. While the Assembly approved a bill extending rent rules, the Senate Majority Leader, does not want to have his house approve a separate bill.

The Senate Majority Leader, who wants to eliminate rent rules in two years while protecting the needy, elderly and disabled, is under pressure from Republicans who have rent-controlled apartments in their districts, the paper said.
